body_markdown:
# Daily Loop-Model Briefing - 2026-11-25

## Outcome

Seven papers were added. Three retrofit pretrained models into loops: Distill to Loop and
LoopFit do it for diffusion Transformers, and LoopDVR does it for dense vision models. Two
companion papers post-train the looped language model Ouro using a teacher extrapolated from
its own loops. SwiftLoop makes looped inference adaptive per position. A theory paper explains
why truncated backpropagation through recurrent depth works and derives an optimizer from that
analysis. None of today's additions cites Benhao Huang's work.

## Added

### Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth

[arXiv:2611.31977](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31977) · Code:
[WinterCCC/Distill-to-Loop](https://github.com/WinterCCC/Distill-to-Loop) (models:
[ShimaRinC/Distill-to-Loop](https://huggingface.co/ShimaRinC/Distill-to-Loop); project page:
[winterccc.github.io/dooop](https://winterccc.github.io/dooop); the paper says the code will be
released with the formal version)

**TL;DR:** Dooop distills a pretrained diffusion Transformer into a looped student that can run
any number of loops at test time; on SD3-medium it matches the teacher with about 37% of the
parameters.

- **Setup:** Students are distilled from SD3-medium (2.03B into 0.756B), SiT-XL/2 on ImageNet-256
  and Z-Image. They are evaluated with GenEval, ImageReward, PickScore and HPSv2.1 (averages
  normalized so the teacher is 100), and with FID on ImageNet. Baselines are the teacher, a
  looped model trained from scratch and ELT.
- **Mechanism / Method:** A few leading and trailing teacher blocks are kept, and the middle
  stack becomes a small set of shared blocks initialized from teacher blocks. Each loop is a
  relaxed fixed-point step on a continuous depth coordinate, and its output is trained toward
  the teacher. Because of this, the loop count can change at test time and higher-order ODE
  solvers can be applied along depth. "Loop guidance" uses an earlier loop's output from the
  same forward pass as the weak model.
- **Results:**
  - At two loops the student averages 100.7 against the teacher's 100, at 29.4 against 50.5
    TFLOPs. Continued training on real data raises this to 105.8.
  - Loop guidance lifts a four-step student from 88.2 to 99.2.
  - On ImageNet, distillation reaches FID 3.785, against 12.573 for a looped model trained
    from scratch and 6.313 with teacher initialization alone.
- **Caveat:** Quality peaks at two to four loops and declines slightly with more, and no
  untied model with the same unique parameters is compared.
- **Why added:** It retrofits a pretrained model into a looped one with test-time-adjustable
  depth, inside a single denoiser call.

### LoopFit: Retrofitting Pretrained Diffusion Transformers with Recurrent Refinement

[arXiv:2611.32175](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32175) · Code: not stated in the paper

**TL;DR:** LoopFit loops the middle blocks of a pretrained diffusion Transformer within each
denoising prediction and steers each pass with the previous pass's per-patch feature change. It
solves 89.8% of boards across 12 visual-puzzle settings.

- **Setup:** A 0.26B pixel-space MMDiT is retrofitted and evaluated on FrozenLake, Maze, TSP and
  Sudoku puzzles and on text-to-image benchmarks. It is compared with larger diffusion and
  vision-language reasoners and with a naive loop that uses uniform deep supervision.
- **Mechanism / Method:**
  - A prelude and coda run once and a shared core runs several passes.
  - Residual Attention Modulation scales and shifts each patch's attention input using how
    much that patch changed on the previous pass.
  - A Residual Relay Loss up-weights patches whose errors persist across passes.
  - At inference, four passes are used at high noise and one at low noise.
- **Results:**
  - Average success is 89.8% against 87.8% for the strongest baseline evaluated on all 12
    settings.
  - On 384 long-path mazes at matched block calls (640 against 646), LoopFit solves 366
    against 165 for a single-pass model that takes more sampling steps.
  - The 4-to-1 pass schedule matches fixed four passes and cuts median batch time by 29.8%.
- **Caveat:** It is a small model evaluated mostly on synthetic puzzles, text-to-image gains are
  small, and the larger baselines were trained differently.
- **Why added:** A looped-core retrofit of a pretrained diffusion model, with extra depth
  compared against extra sampling steps at matched compute.

### LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition

[arXiv:2611.32067](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32067) · Code:
[Intellindust-AI-Lab/LoopDVR](https://github.com/Intellindust-AI-Lab/LoopDVR) (project page:
[siruuui.github.io/LoopDVR](https://siruuui.github.io/LoopDVR/))

**TL;DR:** LoopDVR converts pretrained ViT-based detection, instance segmentation and pose
models into looped networks with about 28% fewer parameters while staying close to the original
accuracy.

- **Setup:** EdgeCrafter detectors, segmenters and pose models at four scales are converted, plus
  DEIMv2. Evaluation is on COCO, against real-time detectors and compression baselines such as
  pruning, low-rank factorization and earlier looped backbones.
- **Mechanism / Method:**
  - Backbone layers are grouped by how different their representations are. Each group reuses
    one block, initialized from its last layer, and the final backbone block stays independent.
  - A per-layer Loop Adapter keeps depth-specific behavior.
  - The looped backbone is distilled from a DINOv3 teacher and paired with a looped decoder.
- **Results:**
  - LoopDet-S reaches 50.9 box AP with 7.0M parameters, against 51.7 at 9.8M for the reference.
  - LoopDet-L keeps 99.3% of the reference AP with 28.4% fewer parameters.
  - LoopSeg-L improves mask AP by 1.0, to 48.1.
  - Removing the Loop Adapters drops LoopDet-S from 50.9 to 49.4 AP.
- **Caveat:** The savings are in stored weights only; FLOPs and latency rise slightly (LoopDet-S:
  53.0 against 50.0 GFLOPs).
- **Why added:** Block reuse with per-iteration adapters, applied to dense vision models.

### The Teacher Is Already Inside: Self-Distilling Looped Language Models Beyond Their Last Loop

[arXiv:2611.32452](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32452) · Code: not stated in the paper

**TL;DR:** ELPSD distills a looped language model's last loop toward a frozen distribution
extrapolated from its first loop through its last, improving math reasoning without any reward
or external teacher.

- **Setup:** Ouro-1.4B-Thinking (a 24-layer stack applied four times per token) is post-trained
  for 100 steps on DeepMath problems. It is evaluated on AIME24-26, MATH-500 and AMC23 against
  GRPO, RLTT and OPSD.
- **Mechanism / Method:** A frozen copy of the model provides the teacher, which extrapolates
  the logits from loop 1 to loop 4. The last loop is trained toward it with exact reverse KL on
  its own rollouts. The paper shows the objective pulls toward the base model's last loop and
  away from its first, and that a teacher recomputed from the current model diverges.
- **Results:**
  - Average avg@8 rises from 61.15 to 63.69, the best on all five benchmarks, against 62.32 for
    GRPO and 61.77 for OPSD.
  - Under RLTT, which spreads the reward over loops, loop-1 entropy collapses from 1.684 to 0.382
    nats.
- **Caveat:** One 1.4B model, math only, 100 steps and a single seed.
- **Why added:** Post-training that exploits the intermediate loops of a looped language model.

### Beyond the Last Loop: Reinforcement Learning with a Teacher Extrapolated from the Model Itself

[arXiv:2611.31939](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31939) · Code: not stated in the paper

**TL;DR:** ELGO adds to GRPO a dense per-token distillation term toward the same loop-extrapolated
teacher, refreshing the teacher as the student catches up.

- **Setup:** The same Ouro-1.4B-Thinking model, data, benchmarks and baselines as the companion
  ELPSD paper by the same author.
- **Mechanism / Method:** The teacher is computed from an anchor copy of the model, which is
  replaced by the current weights once the distillation loss falls below a threshold. The
  outcome reward decides between responses, and the teacher decides which tokens are preferred
  within a response.
- **Results:** Average avg@8 rises from 62.32 with GRPO to 64.20, the best on every benchmark;
  spreading the reward over loops (RLTT) falls to 50.16, below the base model's 61.15.
- **Caveat:** The paper notes it covers one model size, one domain and 100 updates, and the
  baseline numbers are shared with the companion paper.
- **Why added:** RL post-training designed around the loop structure of a looped language model.

### SwiftLoop: Selective Refinement for Adaptive Implicit Reasoning in Looped Transformers

[arXiv:2611.31481](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31481) · Code: not stated in the paper

**TL;DR:** SwiftLoop learns which positions of a looped model can stop updating after each
iteration while their keys and values stay attendable, so compute is spent only where refinement
still matters.

- **Setup:** LOTUS implicit-reasoning models (1B and 3B), Ouro-1.4B and Huginn-0125 (3.5B), on
  GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, GSM-Hard and recurrent prompt prefilling for WinoGrande, ARC-C and
  HellaSwag. It is compared with fixed loop counts and with adaptive and early-exit baselines.
- **Mechanism / Method:** A small predictor reads each position's hidden state and its latest
  change and freezes positions whose score passes a threshold. The predictors are trained offline
  on labels from full trajectories: either how much the position's keys and values would still
  drift, or how much it affects the output margin.
- **Results:**
  - LOTUS-1B keeps 58.83% on GSM8K with 1.80 loops per latent, against 59.29% at six fixed
    loops, about 70% less recurrent compute.
  - Huginn drops from 32 to 12.36-14.07 recurrent steps with accuracy within 0.17 points.
  - Wall-clock speedups reach 2.48x on LOTUS-1B and 1.46-1.82x on Huginn.
- **Caveat:** Predictors and thresholds are fit per model and task, and gains on the 3B models
  are small.
- **Why added:** Adaptive, per-position halting with key-value reuse for looped models.

### How to build and train your recurrent-depth model: A fixed-point perspective

[arXiv:2611.31513](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31513) · Code:
[tmpethick/sparrow](https://github.com/tmpethick/sparrow)

**TL;DR:** The paper shows that input injection in recurrent-depth models is exactly Halpern
iteration, which explains why truncated backpropagation works, and turns the required Lipschitz
constraints into the optimizer Sparrow.

- **Setup:** The theory is followed by experiments on a synthetic SwiGLU teacher task,
  character-level nanoGPT on Tiny Shakespeare, and a small prelude-core-coda looped model trained
  with truncated backpropagation, comparing optimizers such as Muon, MuonH and Aurora.
- **Mechanism / Method:** Additive input injection anchors every step to the input, so a
  Lipschitz block converges with a backpropagation window that does not grow with depth, or grows
  only polylogarithmically with a slowly vanishing step size. Keeping SwiGLU blocks Lipschitz
  requires joint row-norm and spectral-norm constraints, which Sparrow enforces at the cost of
  Muon.
- **Results:**
  - On nanoGPT, Sparrow lowers final validation loss on all 10 seeds by 0.013 and reaches Muon's
    final loss in 1220 instead of 1302 steps.
  - In the looped model it lowers validation loss against Muon at every tested loop count and
    window, by 0.012-0.027.
- **Caveat:** Experiments are tiny, the looped experiment is a three-seed toy model, and the
  optimizer is generic rather than specific to looping.
- **Why added:** Convergence and optimization theory for training recurrent-depth models.

## Catalog update

This run checked one fifth of the existing catalog (90 papers) for publication venue, official
code links and community comment links. No entries changed.

- No paper in this group had a new official proceedings or acceptance page that could be
  confirmed. Several authors list acceptances in their arXiv comments: LoopMoE
  ([2606.04438](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04438)) at EMNLP 2026 and
  [2610.15106](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15106) at a NeurIPS 2026 workshop. These stay
  unchanged until an official record can be checked.
- No arXiv abstract or comment in this group named a new official code repository.

## Near misses

- **SuperFine3D** ([2611.29630](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29630)): reuses one whole refinement
  network across successive resolutions rather than looping layers within a forward pass.
- **Calibrated Reading of Latent Reasoning and Communication**
  ([2611.32143](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32143)): reads continuous chain-of-thought states of
  CODI models, which feed hidden states back as inputs rather than reusing layers.
- **Noise-Level Adjacency in Diffusion Training** ([2611.31605](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31605)):
  studies weight sharing across diffusion noise levels, not layer reuse within a forward pass.
